habitat.naturalHabitat: Human hepatocytes and GI tract (shed in stool)
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen (some non-human primate reservoirs exist but are not clinically significant for most human infection)

identificationClues: Diagnosed by anti-HAV IgM (acute infection) or IgG (past infection/immunity) serology
Non-enveloped, making it notably stable in the environment and resistant to many disinfection methods that work on enveloped viruses
Self-limited illness — does not cause chronic infection, unlike hepatitis B or C

diseases: Acute hepatitis A — typically self-limited; fulminant hepatic failure is rare but can occur, especially with pre-existing liver disease
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral — contaminated food or water, person-to-person contact, particularly in settings with poor sanitation or during outbreaks linked to contaminated food handlers
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Vaccine-preventable; incidence has declined substantially in countries with routine childhood vaccination and improved sanitation, though outbreaks still occur, including among people experiencing homelessness and in foodborne clusters
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Anti-HAV IgM confirms acute/recent infection, while IgG alone (without IgM) indicates past infection or vaccination, not current illness

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Unlike hepatitis B and C, does not cause chronic infection — illness is self-limited
